I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. When I run the same code on Q2, it reproduces all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Item | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | `smb`, 311,694,870 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 241 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | `sw`, 242,903,532 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the most refunds | u81@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 233 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 716,423 KRW |
| h. Growth from August to September | 2.0% |

The Q2 values only matched once I handled three things in the data:

1. **Time zone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (ending in `Z`). I converted it to Korean time (UTC+9) before deciding the quarter and month. Without that, Q2 differed on 6 items, including a 16.0% growth rate instead of 5.3%.
2. **Customer = email:** `customers` has 300 rows but only 250 distinct emails, so the same person can appear under more than one ID. I counted customers by email for b, e and f. Counting by ID gave 278 customers for b in Q2 instead of 233.
3. **Segment names:** the same segment is spelled differently (`'Enterprise '`, `' consumer'`, `'SMB'` and so on), so I trimmed spaces and lowercased them before grouping.

Status was matched only against `'paid'` exactly, and refunds were applied per order line.

STATUS: DONE
